validated_results.title: Alcohol use and the risk of prostate cancer: results from the VITAL cohort study.
validated_results.reason: This prospective VITAL cohort study reports hazard ratios for alcohol consumption and incident prostate cancer in men.

extraction.comparison_type: more than one drink per month vs. no alcohol or less than one drink per month
extraction.population: Men aged 50-76 years in the Vitamins and Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort

sample_size.excerpt: We examined the association between alcohol use and prostate cancer among 34,565 men, 50-76 yr old, in the Vitamins and Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort in Washington State.

cases.excerpt: Incident prostate cancers (n = 816) as of December 31, 2004, were identified through the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results cancer registry.

effect_size.excerpt: Men who consumed more than one drink per month had a small increased risk of prostate cancer (hazard ratio, HR = 1.20; 95% confidence interval, CI = 1.02-1.40) compared with men who drank no alcohol or less than one drink per month.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Men who consumed more than one drink per month had a small increased risk of prostate cancer (hazard ratio, HR = 1.20; 95% confidence interval, CI = 1.02-1.40) compared with men who drank no alcohol or less than one drink per month.

comparison.excerpt: compared with men who drank no alcohol or less than one drink per month

design.excerpt: results from the VITAL cohort study

timing.excerpt: Alcohol consumption was ascertained by baseline questionnaire between October 2000 and December 2002.

continent.excerpt: in the Vitamins and Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort in Washington State

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Alcohol consumption was ascertained by baseline questionnaire
